newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada to pursue trade pacts with South America.
newsitem.headline: Canada to pursue trade pacts with South America.

text.p: Canada plans to explore forging free trade arrangements with major countries in South America, even if it means acting without the United States, Canadian Trade Minister Art Eggleton said on Thursday.
"Brazil is our largest trading partner in South America, so naturally we want to talk to them," Eggleton told reporters in Ottawa a day after meeting U.S. officials in Washington.
"We want to talk about how we can advance bilateral trade and also trade with Mercosur in general."
Mercosur is a free trade pact including Brazil, Argentina, Uruguay and Paraguay. Chile and Bolivia are associate members.
Brazilian Prime Minister Freehand Cords will be in Ottawa in about 10 days, and Eggleton said he would use the opportunity to negotiate freer trade relations in South America.
"I've always been interested in talking with Mercosur, particularly in context of the Free Trade Agreement of the Americas," Eggleton said.

Canada, the United States and Mexico pledged in 1994 to expand free trade throughout the Americas by 2005, starting with Chile. But U.S. President Bill Clinton has been stymied by the Republican-led U.S. Congress, which has refused to give the president fast-track authority to negotiate free trade with Chile.
Meanwhile, Canada has negotiated its own agreement with Chile and now appears to be prepared to explore deals with Brazil and other parts of South America.

"We'll certainly advance our own trade opportunities in Latin America, but I want the United States to be a part of all of this until we reach free trade in the Americas," Eggleton said. "That's ultimately what we're after."
He said his visit to Washington did not give him much hope Clinton would win his fast-track authority soon.
"But that doesn't stop us from talking to these countries," Eggleton said. "I'm going to do what's in the best interest of Canada and Canadians."
